purpose: Authoritative browser gameplay and deployed HTTP latency verification.

production.cleanup: The script left its own two seats in finally and exited successfully.
production.method: Two independent authenticated HTTP clients in a new temporary room. Feedback driving used normal throttle/steering/wipe packets and public snapshots/course geometry. The driver forecast command arrival from measured request latency. No database access or privileged state endpoint.

priorProductionAttempt.termination: Tree DNF; the failed check was reported before the corrected retest.
changesBeforeRetest: Held inputs are evaluated at each 20 ms physics interval, instead of erasing the entire catch-up slice using the final request time.
Hosted HTTP controls hold for at most 1.5 seconds; WebSocket controls retain a 0.5-second limit.
Snapshots expose input acceptance time/hold duration, and snapshot time does not precede simulated state.
The verification driver predicts the pose at command arrival rather than steering from an RTT-old pose.

ordinaryFullCourse.clock: Injected fixture clock; actual HTTP Worker handler and SQLite D1 adapter.

checks: A 1.8-second catch-up matches small steps across the expiry boundary.
Expired controls stop accelerating and speed decays.

fourClientRace.placementScope: Cars/tablets were placed near interactions, an existing tree trunk, and the race finish. Subsequent controls/decisions used real HTTP. The separate full co-op courses used no placements.
checks: Nonfatal car contact and cockpit jolt state.
Door opens on a sustained turn; G closes it.
E drop/retrieve and open-door tablet ejection.
Held tablets stay protected through an open door.
Loose rival tablet can be stolen through an open door.
All four clients agree on race results.
Return to lobby and four-to-two-player mode change.

scopeLimits: Public requests came from two clients on one computer; this was not a manual separate-device browser playtest.
HTTP checks do not validate WebGL pixels, camera feel, audible playback, touch input, or exact native Unity rendering/physics parity.
Tablet privacy is a client rendering rule and is verified separately from the authoritative HTTP tests.
Only stage 04 seed 12345 was driven fully here; all six native profile hashes are covered by separate parity tests.
The full public run verifies authoritative browser rooms, which remain separate from the downloadable Unity/DTLS rooms.
